newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may supply Iraq with 100,000 T wheat.
newsitem.headline: Russia may supply Iraq with 100,000 T wheat.

text.p: Russian organisations are interested in supplying Iraq with 100,000 tonnes of wheat, 50,000 tonnes of sugar and other foodstuffs, Interfax news agency quoted a ministry official as saying on Thursday.

It quoted Igor Bukharov of the Foreign Trade Ministry's department for Asia, Africa and Latin America as saying that supplies of those two foods in those amounts would discussed at a trade cooperation meeting in Baghdad from March 18-20.

The supplies would take place within the framework of the U.N.-sponsored oil-for-food programme, which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise money for humanitarian supplies.
Under the programme, Russian companies have signed contracts to buy a total of 26.2 million barrels of Iraqi oil over a six-month period from December 1996.
Interfax said Russian companies had already bought 3.36 million tonnes (about 23.5 million barrels) of oil worth about $500 million, but it was not clear whether this volume had already been lifted.

Officials at Zarubezhneft, the coordinator of all Russian purchases of Iraqi oil, have declined to comment on total Russian liftings so far. The scheduled meeting in Baghdad would be a session on Russian-Iraqi trade and economic cooperation, Interfax said.
